requirement: Each requirement and example definition badge MUST link to its evidence detail page, and each rendered requirement and example MUST be followed by a "See evidence" link to that page. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and, when an index exists, to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
rationale:
**Verdict:** The sources meet `requirements.index.navigation`: each obligation has marked implementation code and a test. **Implementation, by obligation** - **Definition badge links to its detail page.** `replace_definitions` (src/lib.rs) looks up `plan.detail_path(&full_name)` and renders the anchored badge as ``. When no detail page is planned it falls back to a ``. `DetailPlan::detail_path` and `is_detail_path` (src/index.rs) are marked `{impl}`. The same code handles examples, because the kind comes from the block. - **"See evidence" link.** `replace_definitions` appends `

See evidence

` after each rendered body. Terms are intentionally skipped. They are neither requirements nor examples. - **Detail page links back.** `render_detail_page` (src/index.rs) emits `[View definition](… #habeas--)`. It uses `DefinitionKind::anchor`, which is marked `{impl}` and matches the badge `id`. When `index_path` is `Some`, it also emits `[Requirements index](…)`. It emits no index link otherwise. - **Reference badges keep linking to the definition.** `replace_references` (marked `{impl}`) still produces the anchored `href` to the definition chapter. - **Names containing `.md`.** `chapter_href` (marked `{impl}`) rewrites `.md` to `%2Emd` after swapping the extension for `.html`. Every link goes through it: detail links, definition links, index-table links and reference badges. - I found no unmarked code that implements part of this requirement. The `populate` function in src/index.rs implements other requirements. Its navigation-specific part is the index-table links and detail-chapter attachment, and that part carries an inline `{impl}` marker. **Tests** - `every_definition_gets_a_nested_detail_page_without_an_index` (src/lib.rs) covers: - badge `id` plus `href` for a `req`, an `example`, and a name containing `.md` (`rules.cli.mdbook`, encoded as `%2Emd`); - three "See evidence" links; - the `View definition` back-link, including its `%2Emd` form; - no "Requirements index" link when there is no index. - `index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters` (src/index.rs) covers: - the definition badge `href` to the detail page; - the index table row links; - the detail page's `[Requirements index](…) · [View definition]` header when an index exists. - `links_preserve_requirement_names_containing_md` (src/lib.rs) unit-tests `chapter_href` in both directions. That covers the detail link and the anchored definition link, each with `%2Emd`. - `references_in_nested_chapters_link_to_the_requirement_definition` (src/lib.rs) checks that reference badges still link to the anchored definition. It is tagged `book_badges`, not `navigation`, but it exercises the "continue to link" clause. I found no FIXMEs or acknowledged gaps.
